                                   Over the medium term, economic growth is expected to recover. But
             —Justin Yifu Lin      increased risk aversion, a necessary and desirable tightening of financial
          Chief Economist and      regulations in high-income countries, and measures to reduce the
          Senior Vice President    exposure of developing economies to external shocks are likely to make
                                   finance scarcer and more costly than it was during the boom period.
              The World Bank
                                   As a result, just as the ample liquidity of the early 2000s prompted
                                   an investment boom and an acceleration in developing-country
                                   potential output, higher costs will likely yield a slowing in
                                   developing-country potential growth rates of between 0.2 and 0.7
                                   percentage points, and as much as an 8 percent decline in potential
                                   output over the medium term.

                                   In the longer term, however, developing countries can more than offset
                                   the implications of more expensive international finance by reducing
                                   the cost of capital channeled through their domestic financial markets.
